    Router and Wi‑Fi checklist

    A scan can't see inside your router's settings. Answer these from your router's admin page; each "No" lowers the score. Items marked "auto" were detected by the scanner.

    Where to find these settings

    • Open your router's admin page192.168.1.1Type the gateway address into your browser. The login is often printed on a sticker under the router.
    • Wi‑Fi encryptionWireless › SecurityChoose WPA3‑Personal, or WPA2/WPA3 mixed if older devices must connect. Never WEP or WPA‑TKIP.
    • WPS and UPnPAdvanced › NAT / WPSBoth are convenience features attackers abuse. Turn them off unless something stops working.
    • Remote managementSystem › AdministrationDisable access to the admin page from the internet and any cloud management you don't use.
    • FirmwareSystem › Firmware updateInstall updates and turn on automatic updates. Replace routers the maker no longer updates.
    • Guest / IoT networkWireless › Guest networkPut cameras, plugs, TVs and visitors here so a hacked gadget can't reach your laptop or NAS.

      What this browser reveals

        Every website you visit can read these values. Together they form a fingerprint that can track you without cookies.

        Common default logins to change

        • admin / adminChange nowMany TP‑Link, D‑Link and Netgear models before 2020
        • admin / passwordChange nowOlder Netgear and Linksys routers
        • admin / (blank)Change nowSome older ISP routers and IP cameras
        • admin / 12345Change nowOlder Hikvision cameras before 2017 firmware
        • root / root, root / xc3511Change nowTelnet logins on cheap DVRs used by the Mirai botnet
        • Printed on the stickerBetterUnique per device, but anyone with physical access can read it
        PermissionOnly scan networks you own or have permission to test, such as your home or your company's network with IT's approval. On Wi‑Fi you don't own, such as a guest or hotel network, tick "Just this computer". The scanner refuses public internet addresses and never guesses passwords or runs exploits.
        1. 1

          Get the scanner

          Copy the code below into a file named heimdall_scan.py, or use the file Claude saved for you. It needs Python 3.8+ and nothing else.

        2. 2

          Run one command

          Open Terminal (Mac/Linux) or PowerShell (Windows) in that folder and run the command below. Type YES once to confirm.

          python3 heimdall_scan.py
        3. 3

          Everything is automatic

          Your browser opens the live dashboard at 127.0.0.1:8765 with your real devices. It re-scans on schedule, alerts you to new devices, and saves heimdall_scan.json that you can also load here.

        Build your command

        What it collects

        • Every device on your networkping · TCP · ARPPlus quiet devices from your computer's ARP and IPv6 neighbour tables.
        • Names, makers and modelsmDNS · UPnP · NetBIOS"Living Room TV", "Kari's iPhone", model numbers, Windows names.
        • Open services~100 or 1,024+ portsRemote access, file sharing, cameras, databases, router management.
        • Software versions and web pagesbanners · HTTPOutdated SSH and web servers, login pages without encryption.
        • Certificates and TLSTLS 1.0–1.3Expired or self-signed certificates and outdated protocols.
        • Your Wi‑FiOS Wi‑Fi toolsEncryption type, channel, signal, nearby networks and look-alike networks.

        On iPhone or iPad

        iOS doesn't let apps scan networks, so use the iPhone as the screen. Run the scanner on your computer with --phone (or the "my network" launcher), click Open on phone on the computer and scan the QR code. Or open this page on the iPhone and use Load scan to pick heimdall_scan.json from Files or iCloud Drive.

        On Android

        Install Termux and Termux:API from F‑Droid, save heimdall_scan.py to Downloads, then in Termux run:

        pkg install python termux-api termux-setup-storage python ~/storage/downloads/heimdall_scan.py

        Give Termux:API location permission so Android shares Wi‑Fi names. Android hides other devices' MAC addresses, so makers are identified from names and services instead.

        Phone tips

        • Add to Home ScreenIn Safari or Chrome, use Share › Add to Home Screen to open the dashboard like an app.
        • Same Wi‑Fi onlyPhone viewing works on your home network. Guest and public Wi‑Fi block devices from reaching each other.
        • Tap the mapTap a device once for a summary, twice for its full dossier.
